doc.title: Germaine Bazzle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: Little competition among New Orleans musicians after Katrina
summary: Returning musicians are glad to see each other, so there is joy rather than competition.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Wow. Interesting. In New Orleans, we were talking a little bit on the way in the car about musical opportunities in the various cities. Is there a lot of competition for gigs in the city?

I don’t know so much as competition, I don’t know. I don’t think there’s competition because we don’t have very many musicians back in New Orleans yet. Because everybody, we’re so happy to see each other and we’re so happy to hear each other that we’re not competing with each other. You know the place where I work on Monday nights, some of the musicians, they come in from Texas. One little fellow I think he’s somewhere in Dallas. And he says, “I had to come home, I had to come for at least a weekend, I had to come, I had to come and play.” So you know they walk in with their horns. You know some of them they’re out the case before they get — so we’re not competing at this point anyway. I don’t think that we’re competing as much as we are enjoying each other and welcoming each other. We’re so glad to see each other and share. That’s a very special time, especially since Katrina. It’s all special. So if there’s any competition going on it’s between us and the good Lord because we’re saying come on Lord, give us more, give us more, give us more, let us do more, let us do more. And when I say that it’s coming because I really believe that the music comes from there and goes through — you know we’re just the vessel.

And so we are saying give us more so we can put more of it out, put more of it out. So in that sense I don’t think that we are at that competitive stage. Now maybe when everybody gets back, you know, it might be. But right now it’s just a joyous time.
